questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. One of them said, “Let us use our combined knowledge to bring this animal to life.”

B. On the way, the three friends passed through a forest.

C. Seeing the bones, the friends thought of testing their knowledge and skills.

D. Under a tree in the forest, they saw the bones of an animal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'BDCA'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The initial sentence will be **part B **because the first statement of a para jumble question is usually **a general statement, a noun, a universal fact, or the starting of an incident, etc. **
 
• The given sentence is the start of an incident. Therefore, **part B** will be **the first sentence. **
 
• **Part B** is directly connected with** part D.** While they were passing through the forest they saw the bones of an animal. Hence,** BD** makes a pair. 
 
• **Part C explains part D.** Therefore,** part D **is further connected with part C. 
 
• Only **Option 1 **has these pairs. 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** Option 1. **

 

**Correct Answer:__** *BDCA. *

• The erroneous part **'Did you tell to' should be 'Did you tell' instead. **

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

You had better not to try and feed the animals in the zoo, it is forbidden.

options.text: You had better not to try

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'You had better not to try'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part **'You had better not to try'** should have **'You had better not try'. **
 
• We use had better to refer to** the present or the future**, to talk about actions we think people should do or which are desirable in a specific situation.
 
• The verb form is always **had, not have.**
 
• ** It is followed by the 'infinitive' without 'to'. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***You had better not try** and feed the animals in the zoo, it is forbidden. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The other usage of **'had better'. **

 
 
• We normally shorten it to **’d better** in informal situations. 
 
• **Had better is a strong expression. We use it if we think there will be negative results if someone does not do what is desired or suggested**
 
 
• *Example: **She’d better** get here soon or she’ll miss the opening ceremony. *
